skill.name: next-cache-components-optimizer
skill.description: Optimize Next.js Cache Components routes for instant hard and soft navigation with production-like Playwright tests and verified static-shell refactors.
skill.summary: Build a repeatable test-driven loop that makes Next.js route shells commit instantly and prevents regressions.
skill.author: vercel

security_audit.summary: All 158 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed relative paths, non-secret deployment flags, and official documentation links. No prompt injection, secret collection, arbitrary process execution, path traversal, or data-exfiltration intent was found. The skill provides legitimate Next.js optimization guidance and explicitly keeps its testing API out of production.

content.value_statement: Next.js routes can delay their static shell while dynamic data resolves. This skill builds verified instant-navigation tests and guides Cache Components refactors that preserve behavior.
actual_capabilities: Checks for Next.js 16.3 or newer and enabled Cache Components.
Maps the project build, deployment, authentication, and Playwright test rig.
Creates instant-navigation tests for initial loads and client-side navigation.
Diagnoses blocking awaits, dynamic reads, Suspense placement, and static-shell gaps.
Guides focused refactors that reuse existing loading interfaces and preserve behavior.
Verifies baseline, failure, success, parity, and regression protection.
limitations: Requires Next.js 16.3 or newer with Cache Components enabled.
Requires a production-like build because development mode cannot provide a valid result.
Project-specific authentication, deployment, selectors, and test data still require discovery.
URL-dependent routes may need targeted full prefetching with additional server cost.

use_cases.title: Fix a blocking route
use_cases.description: Identify why a route shell waits for dynamic data, then move blocking work behind focused Suspense boundaries.

use_cases.title: Build a reliable test rig
use_cases.description: Configure a production-like environment that exposes the testing API only outside production and verifies the deployed revision.

use_cases.title: Prevent navigation regressions
use_cases.description: Add hard-navigation and soft-navigation checks that prove meaningful shell content commits before deferred data.

prompt_templates.title: Check one route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the route [ROUTE]. Confirm the Next.js and Cache Components prerequisites, then explain what prevents its static shell from committing instantly.

prompt_templates.title: Create an instant test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright instant-navigation test for [ROUTE] using [NAVIGATION TYPE]. Use an existing static shell marker and verify the test cannot pass vacuously.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize [ROUTE] for hard and soft navigation. Reuse existing loading interfaces, preserve behavior, and verify failure without the fix and success with it.

prompt_templates.title: Establish the complete loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover this repository build and test rig, document its safeguards, optimize [ROUTES] individually, and provide linked evidence for baseline, differential, parity, and final tests.

output_examples.input: Optimize the dashboard route for client-side navigation.
output: The dashboard shell waited for a top-level session read.
The layout and existing chart skeleton now commit immediately.
The locked navigation test fails without the refactor and passes with it.

output_examples.input: Add regression coverage for the initial product-page load.
output_examples.output: The new initial-load check verifies that the product header is served in the static shell while deferred inventory remains gated.

output_examples.input: Review whether the search route can become fully instant.
output_examples.output: The shared shell can commit instantly, but query-specific results require targeted full prefetching or continued streaming.

best_practices: Verify the testing API is enabled for measured builds and disabled for production.
Choose a stable synchronous shell marker that is visible to the actual test account.
Keep a differential result that fails without the fix and passes with it.
anti_patterns: Do not measure instant navigation with development mode, custom timers, or retries.
Do not place one coarse Suspense boundary around the entire route.
Do not ship baseline scaffolding or duplicate existing loading interfaces.

faq.question: Which Next.js versions are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow requires Next.js 16.3 or newer with Cache Components enabled.

faq.question: Can the tests run against next dev?
faq.answer: No. Development mode lacks the production prefetch and locking behavior required for a trustworthy result.

faq.question: Does the skill support both navigation types?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers initial page loads and client-side Link navigation with separate test-driving methods.

faq.question: Will it create new loading skeletons?
faq.answer: It first reuses route loading files, colocated skeletons, or existing Suspense fallbacks.

faq.question: How does it avoid a false passing test?
faq.answer: It establishes an unlocked baseline and can verify that deferred content remains gated while the static shell appears.

faq.question: Can it optimize every dynamic route completely?
faq.answer: No. Some URL-specific content must stream or use targeted full prefetching with an explicit cost tradeoff.
